oil.summary: Crude posted a split session: Brent gained +0.87% to $92.29 and heating oil surged +1.61% to $4.1974/gal on supply-risk headlines, while RBOB cratered -1.62% to $2.5666/gal, weighed down by the US-Russia diesel deal that Lavrov confirmed is pushing refined-product prices lower — US diesel futures reportedly down ~11%. The dominant geopolitical overlay remains the Iran war: Tehran denied any talks with Washington, sending Brent spiking nearly 3% intraday to $93.90 before settling back. Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia reported a 26% jump in October output to 10.563 mb/d, near pre-war levels, capping the upside. Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Ust-Luga Baltic export hub and are reported to have cut Russian refining capacity by 30%. Strait of Hormuz crude flows have recovered to ~80-85% of pre-war levels, but refined-product flows remain stuck near 35%, explaining the crude/product divergence. Options markets price a 77% probability of an OPEC cut at the May 2026 meeting.
drivers: Iran war risk premium: Tehran's denial of Washington talks triggered a sharp intraday Brent spike to $93.90, underscoring how sensitive flat price remains to diplomatic signals.
US-Russia diesel deal depressing refined products: Lavrov confirmed the deal is working, with US diesel futures down ~11%, hammering RBOB and creating a widening crude-vs-product spread.

Supply crosscurrents: Saudi output surges 26% to 10.563 mb/d while Ukrainian drones cut Russian refining capacity by ~30% and hit the Ust-Luga export hub, tightening the global refinery margin picture.

gas.summary: Henry Hub pulled back -2.43% on the day to $3.215/MMBtu, though the contract remains up +8.69% on the week, suggesting the daily retreat is a consolidation rather than a trend reversal. The key geopolitical catalyst is ongoing Iran war uncertainty: European benchmark gas prices rebounded from a one-month low hit Tuesday as markets reassessed supply-route risks through the Strait of Hormuz, where refined-product flows remain far below pre-war norms. Germany's first capacity auction cleared entirely in gas-fired power — all 5.16 GW of derated capacity — signalling structural European gas demand is entrenched. Longer-dated supply diversification plays also gained traction: Turkmenistan revived its $10 billion trans-Caspian pipeline project at an Ashgabat forum, citing the Iran war as a catalyst. Russian strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure add further supply-side noise. Murphy Oil faces a fresh boycott call over Israeli offshore gas licenses.
drivers: Iran war uncertainty driving European gas rebound: European benchmark prices lifted off one-month lows as geopolitical risk returned to the market mid-session.
Germany's capacity auction goes 100% gas: All 5.16 GW awarded to gas-fired projects, cementing near-term European demand support and positive read-across for LNG trade flows.
Turkmenistan trans-Caspian pipeline revival: The Iran conflict is accelerating alternative Central Asian gas route discussions, a potential medium-term structural shift for European supply.

power.summary: EU carbon EUAs edged up +0.56% to $83.88/EUA, broadly flat on the month (+0.24%), as bullish renewable investment news offset bearish macro pressure from the week's -2.08% drift. The session's headline was the RWE-KKR $16 billion UK offshore wind mega-deal, described as likely the largest of its kind in the UK. India approved a 1,150-kilovolt high-capacity transmission corridor worth $7.3 billion to integrate renewables, and Indian turbine manufacturers are in advanced talks on a repowering plan targeting a 50% wind capacity boost without additional land. On the demand-and-infrastructure disruption side, Russia launched 128 attacks on Ukraine's energy grid in a single week, underscoring the vulnerability of centralised power systems. Siemens Energy's record FY2026 revenues and a more-than-tripled dividend reflect strong grid and energy-transition equipment demand. A potential Super El Niño adds an emerging watch item for coal and hydro markets.
drivers: RWE-KKR $16 billion UK offshore wind deal signals large-scale private capital continuing to flow into clean power despite macro uncertainty.
Germany's capacity auction fully cleared by gas projects: Structurally supportive for carbon prices as gas-fired marginal generation keeps EUA demand elevated.
Russia's 128 weekly attacks on Ukraine's grid highlight energy-infrastructure vulnerability and sustain risk premiums across European power and gas markets.
